data.question_intent: Inquire about reasons for flat Financing revenues, RWA density in CIB, and revenue volatility in fixed income and equities.
main_topics: Revenue volatility in fixed income and equities
data.question_quote: Firstly, on Financing revenues, in your footnote, if you strip out the inflation-linked products, I think you said they were flat year on year, whereas a number of US peers called out Financing as being particularly strong year on year. Is there anything you could spell out there in terms of why it's flat?
data.answer_quote: On Financing revenues, what we've basically said is that these are not one-offs, to be clear. There are elements of the Financing portfolio which are somewhat inflation-linked. I think even after we pull those out, there is still some growth in the portfolio, we will come back and confirm that to you. I think this is still a business that we've grown very strongly. We're very happy with the growth in client balances both across Fixed Income Financing and Prime. I would say in Q2, the market was a bit quieter, volatility was a bit lower. We, and I think others, probably saw some compression in margin, but this is still a great business, and remember it [has] a very low RWA density in comparison to the rest of the CIB. So this is a very efficient, high RoTE business, and really what we're looking for there is stability. That's what it's there to provide. Our focus is very much on doing more business with the top 100 clients that we have, and we're convinced that we're seeing growth in those clients in particular.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the question about flat Financing revenues, RWA density in CIB, and revenue volatility in fixed income and equities, providing a high level of evidence with specific figures and explanations.
